results.name: KAYAK Leadership Shift Highlights Booking Holdings AI And Growth Priorities - Simply Wall St News
results.content:
KAYAK has appointed Peer Bueller as CEO, with co founder Steve Hafner moving into a new role focused on artificial intelligence across Booking Holdings. The leadership transition highlights Booking Holdings' increased attention to AI as a core part of its online travel platforms.
February 07, 2026 · Simply Wall St · Reviewed by Bailey Pemberton · KAYAK has appointed Peer Bueller as CEO, with co founder Steve Hafner moving into a new role focused on artificial intelligence across Booking Holdings. The leadership transition highlights Booking Holdings' increased attention to AI as a core part of its online travel platforms.
Giving Hafner a group level AI brief while KAYAK pushes further into business travel helps tie metasearch, fintech style payments, and cross selling across brands like Agoda into a more joined up story about customer retention and higher lifetime value. 🎁 AI focused leadership at the group level could help Booking refine search, recommendations, and trip bundling in ways that support its existing scale advantages over peers such as Expedia Group and Airbnb. 🎁 A CEO with finance and operations experience at KAYAK may support disciplined growth in areas such as KAYAK for Business and Events, which can be attractive for corporate clients.
The leadership change at KAYAK keeps execution in the hands of an insider while freeing co founder Steve Hafner to focus on AI across Booking Holdings, which could matter for how the group competes with Expedia and Airbnb as search and trip planning become more conversational.
Peer Bueller’s background in expansion and KAYAK for Business, together with recent product launches like the Events tool, suggests Booking is trying to deepen its presence in higher value corporate travel rather than relying only on consumer metasearch.

results.name: KAYAK Names Peer Bueller CEO, Steve Hafner Steps Down after
results.content:
KAYAK co-founder Steve Hafner is stepping down as CEO after 22 years. The company named Peer Bueller, KAYAK’s CFO since 2016 and COO since 2021, as the new CEO.
Last update: Feb 06, 2026 · Share · KAYAK co-founder Steve Hafner is stepping down as CEO after 22 years. The company named Peer Bueller, KAYAK’s CFO since 2016 and COO since 2021, as the new CEO. Hafner will move into a newly created executive chair role at KAYAK and also take on a separate role at Booking Holdings focused on AI innovation.
Booking framed Bueller as the executive who has been driving expansion, growing KAYAK for Business, and pushing commercial innovation—signals that the company wants sharper execution on growth and monetization.
KAYAK is a major comparison and discovery tool, so leadership changes can influence how travelers search, how suppliers allocate marketing spend, and which features are prioritized.
Booking’s CEO Glenn Fogel praised Hafner for pioneering metasearch and delivering strong results since Booking bought KAYAK in 2013.

results.name: KAYAK appoints Peer Bueller as Chief Executive Officer
results.content:
Booking Holdings, the world's leading provider of online travel and related services, and parent company of consumer-facing brands including Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK and OpenTable, announced that Peer Bueller has been named Chief Executive Officer of KAYAK.
3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Booking Holdings, the world's leading provider of online travel and related services, and parent company of consumer-facing brands including Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK and OpenTable, announced that Peer Bueller has been named Chief Executive Officer of KAYAK.
Since joining KAYAK, Peer's focus has been on the company's expansion efforts, the growth of KAYAK for Business, the brand's corporate travel platform, and driving commercial innovation. After 22 years as Co-Founder and CEO of KAYAK, Steve Hafner will become Executive Chair of KAYAK, and will take on a new leadership role at Booking Holdings focused on advancing AI innovation to support the company's long term ambitions.
We see a lot of opportunity ahead, and we're well positioned to pursue it," said new KAYAK CEO Peer Bueller.
"Peer is a 14-year Booking Holdings veteran having worked in finance leadership for Booking.com, OpenTable, and KAYAK, and has made a deep impact on our brands' growth and financial operations during his tenure," continued Glenn Fogel. "As CEO of KAYAK, I will continue to focus on making KAYAK everyone's favorite travel app, while raising the bar on our user experience and turning our strategy into results.

results.name: Steve Hafner’s 22-Year Run at Kayak: Skift Timeline
results.content:
Over a 22-year career as CEO of Kayak, Steve Hafner helped spearhead the evolution of online travel and wasn't afraid of taking risks.
Kayak faced significant challenges from Google and the rise of generative AI, impacting its value and prompting strategic pivots. Hafner exited as CEO in 2026, transitioning to a role focused on AI at Booking Holdings, with Peer Bueller succeeding him.
However, increasing pressures from Google and the advent of generative AI led to major challenges, forcing Kayak to pivot back to its software roots. After an attempted buyout and a $457 million writedown, Hafner stepped down as CEO in 2026, moving to a new AI-focused role within Booking Holdings, with Peer Bueller taking over as CEO.

Zmiana na stanowisku CEO Kayak. Współzałożyciel Steve Hafner przekazuje stery, nowym szefem Peer Bueller  
Po ponad 20 latach kierowania Kayak współzałożyciel i wieloletni prezes Steve Hafner ustępuje ze stanowiska operacyjnego. Nowym dyrektorem generalnym należącej do Booking Holdings metawyszukiwarki został Peer Bueller, dotychczasowy dyrektor finansowy i operacyjny. Hafner obejmie funkcję Executive Chair i skoncentruje się na rozwoju innowacji opartych na sztucznej inteligencji w strukturach koncernu.  
Steve Hafner pozostanie związany z Kayak jako Executive Chair. Jednocześnie obejmie nową funkcję w strukturach Booking Holdings, gdzie ma odpowiadać za obszar innowacji, ze szczególnym naciskiem na rozwój rozwiązań opartych na sztucznej inteligencji.  
Hafner współtworzył Kayak w 2004 roku razem z Paulem Englishem, który opuścił firmę w 2013 roku. Od tego czasu kierował spółką, przeprowadzając ją przez kolejne etapy rozwoju, w tym integrację z grupą Booking Holdings.  
Peer Bueller w ostatnich latach odpowiadał za ekspansję spółki, rozwój segmentu Kayak for Business oraz innowacje komercyjne. Jak zapowiada, jego celem jako prezesa będzie dalsze umacnianie pozycji Kayaka jako preferowanej aplikacji podróżniczej, poprawa doświadczeń użytkowników oraz konsekwentna realizacja dotychczasowej strategii wzrostu.  
Zmiana wpisuje się w szersze działania Booking Holdings związane z transformacją technologiczną i rosnącą rolą AI w sektorze turystycznym. MBG
